speaker: nick_sorrell
text: The orchard, sir. His last word and my first come too close. I have gone in a breath early twice. I would have a clearer lead, if the book can spare it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: It went, Will. The yard wept. A boy who is forgiven does not need a new cue on Monday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He needs it because it went. I have seen a fraction of doubt spread through a scene like a crack through a pane, and the orchard is all pane.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I am not asking a new speech. I am asking not to stand on the breath before the word.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then say what you would add. I will hear whether it is caution or carpentry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two words, and not a speech. They are for the roll, Nick, not for a yard that will walk off with them in its mouth. Thou comest on the second of them. Not on the breath before it.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: The second. I can hold for the second. I could not hold for the end of the first while the yard was still in it.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Two words, then. They go into the book and into both rolls before any man leaves with the old cue in his mouth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Mark them, Humphrey. The book, and both rolls. Your small sign in the corner. I will not have a rival memory walked out of this yard.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: The book, and the two rolls, and not a third for kindness. A third copy is how the old cue gets out of the yard.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Give them me on the roll. I will not love them out of duty, and I will not say them into the room.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They are written. Try them from the roll, and do not give the yard a copy in your mouth.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: It is better. The boy has a step in it, and I have an end.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I will not come early on it. If the book says the second word, I come on the second word.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Nick. The lute. The song is not this cue, and the morning is not all orchard. Come when the ink is dry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Go to him, Nick. The two words are in Humphrey's hand. Thou art not to stand over the roll and improve them.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I am going. The second word, and then the lute. I will not sing the cue.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: And you will keep the note you kept on Saturday. The lute is a measure. It is not a dare.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The rest of the morning is the king. Tomorrow is a floor, not a yard. I would have the book we are taking, and not a book the yard has never heard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The book we take this morning is the book Shoreditch has. The other leaves stay in the chest until the house asks for them by name. I am not rehearsing them into a Monday.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Then I mark the two words, and I do not open the chest. The small sign goes on these three. It does not go on anything that was cut.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Fair. It is better. I have said so. I will not make it a speech.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twice is enough. Nick, the lute. Humphrey, the rolls. Dick, the king the yard already knows. The chest can wait for the man who sent for it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: The lute is this way. Bring the voice you mean to keep.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I have it under the note. I am not spending it on a cue.
